answer.rationale: Rollback is ruled out by compliance (memory_b1 shows rollback was effective but is now prohibited). Regional failover (memory_b2) risks disrupting settlement traffic at peak, and its benefit was demonstrated for a latency degradation of a different character. Adding capacity is slow and doesn't address the write-path contention cause. Enabling a circuit breaker (memory_b4) would shed load on a dependency, but the problem is internal write-path latency, not a partner outage. Routing read-oriented settlement queries and dashboard/report traffic to read replicas (memory_b5) directly reduces primary-node load, letting the write path recover without touching the security-patched release and without failing any customer writes. I will verify memory_b5 (read-replica routing recovered write latency same-day) and memory_b2 (regional failover restores latency fast) as a fallback if read-replica routing proves insufficient. First step is a small guarded canary of the replica routing to confirm latency improvement before widening.
